```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Packages needed (install once):
# install.packages(c("flexdashboard", "shiny", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "readr", "DT", "jsonlite"))
library(flexdashboard)
library(shiny)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(DT)
library(jsonlite)

OUT_DIR    <- "outputs"                       # folder created by the Python notebook
TEST_START <- as.POSIXct("2019-11-12 14:08:25", tz = "UTC")   # start of the out-of-sample test period

scores  <- read_csv(file.path(OUT_DIR, "dashboard_scores.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
quality <- read_csv(file.path(OUT_DIR, "dashboard_quality.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
model   <- fromJSON(file.path(OUT_DIR, "model_export.json"), simplifyVector = FALSE)

scores$timestamp <- as.POSIXct(scores$timestamp, tz = "UTC")
scores <- scores %>% arrange(name, timestamp)
stocks <- sort(unique(scores$name))
THRESHOLD <- model$threshold
FEATS <- unlist(model$features)

# ---- portable model (exported from the Python notebook) --------------------------------
walk_tree <- function(tr, x) {
  node <- 1L
  while (tr$left[node] != -1) {
    f <- tr$feature[node] + 1L
    if (x[f] <= tr$threshold[node]) node <- tr$left[node] + 1L else node <- tr$right[node] + 1L
  }
  tr$value[node]
}

prep_trees <- function(trees) {
  lapply(trees, function(t) list(left = unlist(t$left), right = unlist(t$right),
                                 feature = unlist(t$feature), threshold = unlist(t$threshold),
                                 value = unlist(t$value)))
}
if (!is.null(model$trees)) model$trees <- prep_trees(model$trees)

predict_prob <- function(x) {   # x: numeric vector in the order of model$features
  if (model$type == "lr") {
    z <- model$intercept + sum(unlist(model$coef) * (x - unlist(model$mean)) / unlist(model$scale))
    return(1 / (1 + exp(-z)))
  }
  if (model$type == "rf") {
    return(mean(vapply(model$trees, walk_tree, numeric(1), x = x)))
  }
  raw <- model$init + model$learning_rate * sum(vapply(model$trees, walk_tree, numeric(1), x = x))
  1 / (1 + exp(-raw))
}

# Features at the LAST observation of a holder-count vector (same definitions as the notebook)
last_features <- function(v) {
  n   <- length(v)
  chg <- c(NA, diff(v))
  gr  <- chg / c(NA, v[-n])
  gr[!is.finite(gr)] <- NA
  c(prev_popularity_change = chg[n],
    prev_growth_rate       = gr[n],
    prev_rolling_avg       = mean(v[(n - 6):n]),
    prev_momentum          = v[n] - v[n - 7],
    prev_users_holding     = v[n],
    down_count_7           = sum(chg[(n - 6):n] < 0),
    growth_vol_7           = sd(gr[(n - 6):n]))
}

backtest <- function(d) {
  x <- d %>% filter(!is.na(probability), !is.na(next_decrease))
  if (nrow(x) == 0) return(NULL)
  actual <- sum(x$next_decrease == 1)
  alerts <- sum(x$alert == 1)
  hits   <- sum(x$alert == 1 & x$next_decrease == 1)
  list(n = nrow(x), actual = actual, alerts = alerts, hits = hits,
       precision = ifelse(alerts > 0, hits / alerts, NA),
       recall    = ifelse(actual > 0, hits / actual, NA),
       base_rate = actual / nrow(x))
}

img_path <- function(fn) file.path(OUT_DIR, fn)
img_render <- function(fn) {
  renderImage({
    validate(need(file.exists(img_path(fn)), paste(fn, "not found in the outputs folder - run the notebook first.")))
    list(src = img_path(fn), contentType = "image/png", width = "100%")
  }, deleteFile = FALSE)
}
```

```{r}
selectInput("stock", "Stock", choices = stocks, selected = if ("ARKK" %in% stocks) "ARKK" else stocks[1])
sliderInput("window", "Observations to display", min = 100, max = 3000, value = 500, step = 100)
checkboxInput("oos", "Back-test on the out-of-sample test period only", value = TRUE)
helpText("The model was trained on data before 12 Nov 2019. Scores before that date are in-sample and optimistic.")

```

```{r}
stock_data <- reactive({
  scores %>% filter(name == input$stock) %>% arrange(timestamp)
})
```

-------------------------------------

### Latest holders

```{r}
renderValueBox({
  d <- stock_data(); valueBox(format(tail(d$users_holding, 1), big.mark = ","), icon = "fa-users")
})
```

### Probability of a decrease (next observation)

```{r}
renderValueBox({
  p <- tail(stock_data()$probability, 1)
  valueBox(ifelse(is.na(p), "n/a", paste0(round(100 * p, 1), "%")), icon = "fa-percent")
})
```

### Risk label

```{r}
renderValueBox({
  p <- tail(stock_data()$probability, 1)
  lab <- ifelse(is.na(p), "Insufficient history", ifelse(p >= THRESHOLD, "High risk", "Low risk"))
  valueBox(lab, icon = "fa-exclamation-triangle",
           color = ifelse(lab == "High risk", "danger", ifelse(lab == "Low risk", "success", "warning")))
})
```

### Last reading

```{r}
renderValueBox({
  valueBox(format(tail(stock_data()$timestamp, 1), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), icon = "fa-clock")
})
```

### Data-quality check

```{r}
renderUI({
  q <- quality %>% filter(name == input$stock)
  if (nrow(q) == 1 && q$data_quality_flag == 1) {
    div(class = "alert alert-warning",
        strong("Data-quality warning: "), q$flag_reason,
        ". Predictions for this stock are not reliable.")
  } else {
    div(class = "alert alert-success", "No data-quality flags for this stock.")
  }
})
```

### Predicted probability of a decrease at the next observation

```{r}
renderPlot({
  d <- tail(stock_data(), input$window)
  ggplot(d, aes(timestamp, probability)) + geom_line(colour = "steelblue") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = THRESHOLD, colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point(data = filter(d, next_decrease == 1), aes(y = 0.02), size = 1) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Probability",
         subtitle = "Red dashed line = decision threshold; black dots = a decrease actually followed") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
})
```

Row
-------------------------------------

### Back-test for this stock

```{r}
renderTable({
  d <- stock_data()
  if (isTRUE(input$oos)) d <- d %>% filter(timestamp >= TEST_START)
  b <- backtest(d)
  if (is.null(b)) return(data.frame(Message = "No scored observations in the selected period."))
  data.frame(Measure = c("Observations scored", "Actual decreases", "Base rate of decreases",
                         "Alerts raised", "Alerts that were correct", "Precision", "Recall"),
             Value = c(format(b$n, big.mark = ","), format(b$actual, big.mark = ","),
                       sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * b$base_rate), format(b$alerts, big.mark = ","),
                       format(b$hits, big.mark = ","),
                       ifelse(is.na(b$precision), "n/a", sprintf("%.2f", b$precision)),
                       ifelse(is.na(b$recall), "n/a", sprintf("%.2f", b$recall))))
})
```

Watchlist
=====================================

Row
-------------------------------------

### Latest risk signal for every stock (scores the most recent reading in the data file)

```{r}
watch <- scores %>%
  group_by(name) %>% slice_tail(n = 1) %>% ungroup() %>%
  left_join(quality %>% select(name, data_quality_flag, flag_reason), by = "name") %>%
  transmute(Stock = name,
            `Last reading` = format(timestamp, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"),
            Holders = users_holding,
            `Probability of decrease` = round(probability, 4),
            Label = ifelse(is.na(probability), "Insufficient history", ifelse(probability >= THRESHOLD, "High risk", "Low risk")),
            `Data-quality flag` = ifelse(data_quality_flag == 1, "FLAGGED", ""),
            Reason = ifelse(is.na(flag_reason), "", flag_reason)) %>%
  arrange(desc(`Probability of decrease`))

DT::renderDataTable({
  DT::datatable(watch, rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 15, scrollX = TRUE))
})
```

Row
-------------------------------------

### Note

The data end in February 2020, so these are historical illustrations, not live signals. A high probability
means the model expects the number of holders to fall at the next observation. It is a proxy for financial
risk, not a prediction of investor loss.

```{r}
              value = "1200, 1203, 1203, 1199, 1195, 1195, 1190, 1188, 1188, 1185, 1180, 1181, 1176, 1170, 1170, 1166, 1160")
```

Row
-------------------------------------

### Result

```{r}
result <- eventReactive(input$go, {
  v <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(strsplit(gsub("[,;\n\t]", " ", input$counts), " +")[[1]]))
  v <- v[!is.na(v)]
  if (length(v) < 16) stop(paste0("Please provide at least 16 consecutive observations (you gave ", length(v), ")."))
  if (any(v < 0)) stop("Holder counts cannot be negative.")
  f <- last_features(v)
  if (any(is.na(f))) stop("Not enough valid history: the counts contain zeros or too little variation to compute all features.")
  p <- predict_prob(as.numeric(f[FEATS]))
  list(p = p, f = f)
}, ignoreNULL = FALSE)

renderUI({
  r <- tryCatch(result(), error = function(e) e)
  if (inherits(r, "error")) return(div(class = "alert alert-danger", conditionMessage(r)))
  lab <- ifelse(r$p >= THRESHOLD, "High risk", "Low risk")
  tagList(
    h3(paste0("Probability of a decrease at the next observation: ", round(100 * r$p, 1), "%")),
    h3(paste0("Risk label: ", lab)),
    p("Features computed from the last observation:"),
    tags$table(class = "table table-condensed", style = "width:auto;",
      tags$tbody(lapply(names(r$f), function(n) tags$tr(tags$td(n), tags$td(round(r$f[[n]], 4))))))
  )
})
```

Row
-------------------------------------

### Caution

Headline scores that include the stock CIG are inflated by a data-feed artifact (its holder count alternates
between about 3 and about 3,500 every hour from around August 2019). The results without CIG are the more
credible estimate of predictive ability.

About and limitations
=====================================

Row
-------------------------------------

### What this dashboard does

It shows the output of the model trained in the capstone notebook. For a chosen stock it displays the
probability that the number of users holding the stock will **decrease at the next observation**, a risk label
based on the decision threshold, and a back-test against what actually happened.

**What the risk label means.** Risk = 1 when the number of users holding a stock decreased compared with the
previous observation; Risk = 0 when it stayed the same or increased. This is a **proxy** for financial risk.
The dataset has no prices, trades, returns or investor identities, so a High-risk label does not mean that any
investor lost money.

**Limitations.**

* Aggregate holder counts for 31 Robinhood stocks, May 2018 to February 2020; not South African data.
* One stock (CIG) shows an implausible hourly pattern that inflates scores; CIG and XOXO are flagged.
* Observations are roughly hourly with irregular gaps, so "the next observation" is not always the next hour.
* A prototype evaluated on one chronological test period. It is not investment advice and is not ready for deployment.
